name: Leg extension
cue: Lean back; lower slowly into a deep bend.
research: v10 (science audit A6, 4 Oct 2026): reclined. Training the leg extension at a hip angle of 40 deg grew the rectus femoris clearly more than at 90 deg, with the vastus lateralis the same (Larsen 2025), and the initial-range (deep-knee) half grew more than the final half (Pedrosa 2022); it is the program's main rectus femoris builder (+13.2% vs +1.1% for the leg press, Kinoshita 2026). So the back pad is set as far back as the machine goes: pelvis reclined 40 deg (trunk -42, back pad 40 deg back from vertical through the sacrum and the upper back), thighs level on the seat (hip flexion 50, v9 72), knee joint on the machine pivot, knee 100 -> 5 (starting from the deepest bend), ankle ~5 deg dorsiflexion, roller 2.5-5 cm above the ankle, top hold 0.2 s (v9 0.5); cue "Lean back; lower slowly into a deep bend." The hip-joint centre stays where v9 had it, so the knee axis stays on the lever hub; reclining the pelvis rolls the sit bones 2.4 cm forward under the hips, and the seat pin follows them (the seat pad, its rounded front edge ~6 cm behind the knee axis so the calf clears it at 100 deg, is unchanged). Hands: with the trunk reclined the upper arms hang almost straight down (shoulder extension ~40 relative to the trunk, elbow ~64) and the hands hold upright grips beside the hips at hip-joint level, perpendicular to the forearms (neutral wrist); forearms and fists stay behind the thighs, so they never cover the quads, and the narrower back pad (0.17 H) lets the upper arms hang past its edges. Load: a cam on the knee-axis hub (it turns with the lever) winds a cable that runs straight down to a guided stack beside the tower; the stack rises 0.05 H per radian of knee extension. Geometry: tools/design/leg_extension_v10.mjs (loads: tools/design/loads.mjs)

camera.note: Research view is the lateral profile (az 90). az 80 stays 10 deg off it; raised 14 deg so the anterior thigh (the quads face up on the horizontal thighs) reads along its whole length, with rectus femoris between vastus lateralis and medialis. A more frontal azimuth foreshortened the thighs into blobs.
